column1: # Tag audit proposals — tranche 5: every 8th flag by code at offset 4 (32 of 254).
# Additions and aliases; removals are their own round. See #174.
# HOW TO REVIEW: delete the rows you disagree with. What survives is applied.
# Nothing else to fill in; the deletions are themselves the record of your call.
# The pull request shows each flag's image beside its row.
# Then say so, and the agent runs scripts/apply-tag-audit.mjs, the validators and
# the Playwright suite. Do not edit proposals.original.tsv — the difference
# between it and this file is how your rejections get remembered.
# Read the name; the code beside it is what the script applies to, and a row whose
# name and code disagree is refused. To see a flag: https://flagfilter.com/?q=<name>
# Columns: name, code, tag or alias, add|remove|alias, confidence, why.

column6: The three dolphins are on a white shield.
The figures, tree and tools stand around a shield showing tools and a ship.
The Bible, cross and flags are on a shield.
A laurel branch and a palm frond frame the shield.
Bolivian flags flank the arms, the way standards flank Ecuador's.
Rifles, cannons and an axe stand behind the oval.
The axe is a tool as well as a weapon, by the axe rule.
A condor stands on top of the arms.
The condor, and an alpaca inside the oval.
BOLIVIA is written on the oval.
The oval spells out the country's name.
Ten stars run round the bottom of the oval.
The oval shows Cerro Rico, the silver mountain of Potosí.
A breadfruit tree and a wheat sheaf inside the oval, and laurel and olive branches outside.
A red Phrygian cap is raised on the left of the arms.
A sun hangs in the sky above the mountain, drawn as a small ring.
A small chapel with a tower stands on the lower hill: the Chapel of the Sacred Heart of Jesus.
The sun is drawn as a closed ring, which the sun rule counts, like Kyrgyzstan's ring; it is small.
The George Cross shows Saint George on horseback; the figure is small.
Saint George's lance on the George Cross.
